**Overall:** 45d window has 205 trades at -0.29R (CI -0.43..-0.14), P&L -2174. The lab is losing, but the random-entry control is at -0.13R (n=31, CI -0.51..+0.20). Almost no family is separable from the control yet.

**Exit anatomy:** Stops are 112 of 205 trades at -1.06R. Targets (+1.62R), signals (+0.47R) and time exits (+0.34R) are positive. Entries are poor, with a 33% win rate. Shorts are +0.15R (n=37, 57% win) and longs -0.38R (n=168). That fits the weak tape (SPY -6% vs SMA50, BTC -12.5%), where long-biased mean reversion and breakout entries get run over. The long/short gap is suggestive but not tested.

**Families:**
- vwap_revert#1 is the one clear loser. n=35, -0.54R, CI -0.87..-0.18, entirely below zero and below the control. Win rate is 17%, drawdown 46%, and it is already on probation. I propose retiring it.
- squeeze#2 is +0.87R, but n=6 and the CI spans zero (-0.43..+2.17). The three wins were crypto longs at +2.8R each. It is promising but unproven. squeeze#1, the same family with other parameters, is -0.42R, so the family edge is not established.
- meanrev_bb#2 is -0.12R (n=60, 52% win) with PF 0.62. It wins often but loses big, so the stop/target asymmetry is poor. Its last 30 trades are +0.02R, so it is flat rather than broken.
- crypto_mtf#1 (-0.47R, 9% win, n=11), trend_ema (-0.55R, 0 wins, n=7) and breakout_orb (-0.94R, n=7) are all too small to judge. Each looks bad, though.
- The allocator gives 0.20 to trend_ema#2, which has n=1, and 0.15 to breakout_orb#2, which has n=3 and -1.16R. Capital is going to unproven variants. This is an allocator issue to watch.

**Features:** The top-feature bins are mostly noisy, with n≈41 per bin and non-monotonic patterns, so I am not acting on them. Weekend and Sunday/Saturday results (+0.2 to +0.6R) have n≤13, which is noise. The Mon/Tue weakness (-0.5R, n=122 combined) is the only pattern with a decent sample. It is probably regime-driven rather than structural, so I am not filtering on it yet.

**Testing:** I ran no backtests this session because of the tight budget. The proposal rests on live-trade evidence only.

**Proposal:** Retire vwap_revert#1. It has the strongest negative evidence in the lab and a drawdown that is out of line.

proposals.rationale: n=35, expectancy -0.54R, CI -0.87..-0.18 (entirely negative), 17% win, PF 0.27, maxDD 46%. Worse than the random-entry control (-0.13R) and on probation. The evidence supports retiring it.

structured_output.memory_update_md:
## Lab memory (as of 2026-10-09)
- Baseline: 45d, 205 trades, -0.29R (CI -0.43..-0.14). Random-entry control -0.13R (n=31, CI -0.51..+0.20). Nearly no family is separable from the control yet.
- Exit anatomy: stops are 55% of trades at -1.06R; targets +1.62R, signals +0.47R, time +0.34R. Entry quality is poor (33% win rate).
- Shorts +0.15R (n=37) vs longs -0.38R (n=168) in a weak tape (SPY -6% vs SMA50, BTC -12.5%). HYPOTHESIS, untested: long-biased entries are hurt in downtrends. A regime/side filter is worth testing when the sample grows.
- vwap_revert#1: n=35, -0.54R, CI fully negative. Proposed retire 10-09 (status: pending).
- squeeze#2: +0.87R but n=6, CI spans zero (crypto long wins at about +2.8R each). squeeze#1 is -0.42R (n=18). Watch; do not trust yet.
- meanrev_bb#2: wins often (52%) but PF 0.62, so stop/target asymmetry is poor; last 30 trades ~0R. A wider-target or tighter-stop param test is a candidate.
- Allocator gives 0.20 to trend_ema#2 (n=1) and 0.15 to breakout_orb#2 (n=3, -1.16R): capital on unproven variants. Watch.
- Feature bins (rsi_2, atr_pct, dow, hour) are noisy at n≈41 per bin; no action. Mon/Tue weakness (-0.5R, n=122) is only a sample-adequate pattern, likely regime.
- No backtests were run in the 10-09 session (budget $1.5). Next session: backtest meanrev_bb#2 variants and a side/regime filter, and compare against random_entry.
